title: Interfacial Charge Transport in ZnO-Based Metal-Insulator-Metal Devices Probed by Electron-Beam-Induced Current
content: Memristive devices, typically realized in a metal-insulator-metal configuration, are emerging as key candidates for next-generation non-volatile memory, logic operations, and neuromorphic computing. Their electrically tunable resistive states and potential for high-density integration make them particularly attractive for advanced electronic applications [1]. The layer stack configuration plays a crucial role in governing the conduction mechanism, thereby influencing overall device performance [2]. Similar junctions have historically been studied primarily in semiconductors to map depletion regions, recombination sites, and bias-dependent transport characteristics [3]. However, with the advent of high-resolution scanning electron microscopy, cross-sectional electron beam-induced current (EBIC) has emerged as a powerful technique for probing interfacial phenomena in thin films [4, 5]
